inputs.question: What changed in AI agent evaluation research and tooling this month?

outputs.reference: A three-section brief citing recent agent-evaluation papers and practitioner discussion with URLs.

paper | The Necessity of a Unified Framework for LLM-Based Agent Evaluation | 2026-02-03 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03238
paper | AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Feedback | 2025-05-05 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02820
hn | Dayjob: Tax - evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments | 2026-10-28 | https://surgehq.ai/blog/dayjob-tax
hn | Red-teaming AI agent monitors with an LLM that fakes tool outputs | 2026-10-25 | https://www.redwoodresearch.org/blog/simulated-con

brief.answer:
## What changed
Practitioners are moving from static benchmarks to task-level evaluation: Surge's Dayjob: Tax scores agents on 50 professional tax assignments (https://surgehq.ai/blog/dayjob-tax), and Redwood red-teams agent monitors with simulated tool outputs (https://www.redwoodresearch.org/blog/simulated-con). Research argues for a unified agent-evaluation framework (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03238). LangSmith shipped 0.14.14 (https://pypi.org/project/langsmith/0.14.14/).

## Why it matters
Our gates score tool use and oversight on small datasets; task-level suites and monitor red-teaming are the next maturity step. Evidence on monitors rests on one blog post.

## Recommended follow-ups
Pilot a task-level suite for one agent; review AutoLibra's metric induction (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02820).

## Why it matters
Both are patch releases on the versions the factory builds on, so they are likely fixes. The release feed has no notes, so impact is unverified; one practitioner write-up explains how Deep Agents sit on LangGraph (https://www.tamirdresher.com/blog/2026/10/10/what-langgraph-actually-builds).

## Recommended follow-ups
Read the changelogs, bump in a branch, and let the eval gates decide.

outputs.reference: Cites recent work questioning LLM-as-a-judge reliability for rubric scoring and recommends pairing it with code evaluators.

hn_query: LLM as judge

paper | Systematic Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge in LLM Alignment Tasks | 2024-08-23 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13006
hn | no relevant stories in the window

brief.answer:
## What changed
Recent work questions whether an LLM judge can reliably verify rubrics in agentic tasks (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29920), extending earlier findings on judge sensitivity to prompt templates (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13006).

## Why it matters
A judge alone is not reliable enough to gate releases. Our gates use code evaluators for tool use, oversight, and policy, with a judge as an optional signal, which matches the evidence. Practitioner discussion this month was thin.

## Recommended follow-ups
Keep code evaluators as the gate; calibrate any judge against human labels before it can block a promotion.
